versions.change: First release of AXI specification v1.0
First release of AXI specification v2.0 (defines AXI4 and AXI4-Lite)
Public beta draft of AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification
First release of AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification; integrates AXI3 and AXI4 definitions presented separately in Issue C; first description of AXI Coherency Extensions (ACE)
Second release; adds clarifications, recommendations, and new capabilities. Compatibility maintained via property declarations.
EAC-0 release of version F. New AMBA 5 interfaces defined: AXI5, AXI5-Lite, ACE5, ACE5-Lite, ACE5-LiteDVM, ACE5-LiteACP.
EAC-1 release to address issues found with EAC-0; no content change vs EAC-0.
EAC-0 release of version G. New optional features defined for AMBA 5 interface variants. Multi_Copy_Atomicity property required to be True from Issue G onward.
EAC-0 release of version H. New optional features defined for AMBA 5 interface variants.

deprecated_features.rationale: AXI4 enforces single-master-ordered write data on the W channel; per-beat ID tagging on write data no longer required.
Removed because most components do not require locked transactions, and locked transactions significantly increase interconnect complexity and reduce ability to make QoS guarantees.

deprecated_features.feature: Write data interleaving (multiple WID streams interleaved on W channel)
deprecated_features.rationale: Deprecated in AXI4 and later. See AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification issue F for details on AXI3 write data interleaving.

backward_compat_traps.axi3: AxLEN[3:0] — Burst_Length = AxLEN[3:0] + 1; burst length 1-16 transfers for all burst types
backward_compat_traps.axi4: AxLEN[7:0] — Burst_Length = AxLEN[7:0] + 1; INCR up to 256 transfers, FIXED/WRAP still 1-16

backward_compat_traps.axi3: WID signal present on W channel; tags each write data beat with originating ID; write data interleaving permitted
backward_compat_traps.axi4: WID removed; write data must be issued in same order as addresses; no interleaving

AxCACHE[3:0] bit allocations renamed: AWCACHE = {Allocate, Other Allocate, Modifiable, Bufferable}; ARCACHE = {Other Allocate, Allocate, Modifiable, Bufferable}. Some memory types have different encodings between AXI3 and AXI4 (see Table A4-5).

backward_compat_traps.axi3: AWQOS, ARQOS, AWREGION, ARREGION, AWUSER, ARUSER, WUSER, BUSER, RUSER all NOT implemented
backward_compat_traps.axi4: All present (QoS, region, user-defined extensions added)

backward_compat_traps.axi3: Slave must wait for WVALID/WREADY/WLAST before asserting BVALID. BVALID independent of AW handshake (i.e. AW need not be acknowledged before W completes).
backward_compat_traps.axi4: Slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, WREADY (and WLAST) ALL asserted before asserting BVALID. Reflects expected AXI3 usage but is now mandatory.

backward_compat_traps.axi3: Ordering of Device transactions with same ID to same slave is NOT an explicit requirement.
backward_compat_traps.axi4: All Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other.

backward_compat_traps.axi3: Master may issue ARLOCK=2'b10 / AWLOCK=2'b10 (Locked access)
backward_compat_traps.axi4: Any AXI3 locked transaction is converted: AWLOCK[1:0]=0b10 -> normal write (AWLOCK=0b0); ARLOCK[1:0]=0b10 -> normal read (ARLOCK=0b0). Components that cannot tolerate this translation cannot be used in AXI4.

fields.version_naming_history_note: AXI specification versions v1.0 and v2.0 (used in Issues B and C) have been discontinued to avoid confusion with AXI3 / AXI4. Issue E.a was originally published as Issue E.

evidence.quote: 16 June 2003 / A / Non-Confidential / First release; 19 March 2004 / B / First release of AXI specification v1.0; 03 March 2010 / C / First release of AXI specification v2.0; 28 October 2011 / D / First release of AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification; 22 February 2013 / E / Second release; 18 December 2017 / F / EAC-0 release: AXI5, AXI5-Lite, ACE5, ACE5-Lite, ACE5-LiteDVM, ACE5-LiteACP; 30 July 2019 / G / EAC-0; 31 March 2020 / H / EAC-0
WID — The ID tag of the write data transfer. Implemented in AXI3 only.

AXI3 supports burst lengths of 1-16 transfers, for all burst types. AXI4 extends burst length support for the INCR burst type to 1-256 transfers. Support for all other burst types in AXI4 remains at 1-16 transfers. Burst_Length = AxLEN[3:0]+1 (AXI3); Burst_Length = AxLEN[7:0]+1 (AXI4).
AXI4 does not support locked transactions. However, an AXI3 implementation must support locked transactions.

In an AXI4 environment, any AXI3 locked transaction is converted as follows: AWLOCK[1:0] = 0b10 is converted to a normal write transaction, AWLOCK = 0b0; ARLOCK[1:0] = 0b10 is converted to a normal read transaction, ARLOCK = 0b0.
In AXI4, all Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other. This ordering is not an explicit requirement of AXI3.
The interleaving of write data with different IDs was permitted in AXI3, but is deprecated in AXI4 and later.
It is required that the Multi_Copy_Atomicity property is True for Issue G and later of this specification.
